title: Stale-bounce gate is bypassable: the contact-fallback leg treats a pre-correction bounce as genuine when the corrected channel is unchanged — fabricates referee_contact_invalid on a contact never re-tried
evidence: webhooks.gleam: 'The contact-fallback match (no send id — the crash-mid-tick edge) is treated as genuine.' followed by 'case row.matched_send_at == "" || row.send_is_post_correction { True -> exhaust_row('; find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql fallback: 'OR ($2 <> '' AND CASE WHEN rc.correction_cycles >= 1 THEN NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, '') ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, ''), rc.contact_email) END = $2)'
detail: AC3b/W1: sweep is send-then-claim, so a crash-mid-tick send has no attempts entry; matched_send_at='' is hardcoded genuine. A stale redelivered pre-correction bounce whose envelope equals the corrected (unchanged) email/phone exhausts the row and stamps referee_contact_invalid even though the corrected contact was never re-tried — the exact fabrication W1's comment says the gate prevents.
recommended_fix: In the cycles>=1 fallback arms, require NULLIF(corrected_email,'') IS DISTINCT FROM contact_email (same for phone); an unchanged channel cannot distinguish the stale bounce, so stand down.

title: One-cycle rule has no SQL backstop: mark_awaiting_correction's WHERE matches a corrected row (queued, cycles=1, not taken over) — the AD-7 guard rests solely on the two Gleam call-site cycles gates
evidence: mark_awaiting_correction.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status IN (''queued'', ''contact_initiated'') AND taken_over_at IS NULL' — no correction_cycles arm; correct_reference_call.sql comment claims 'correction_cycles bumps to 1 (max by construction)'
detail: The r2 blocker's parallel hole (failure path re-entering the loop) was fixed structurally in SQL (taken_over_at IS NULL); the AD-7 cycle cap has no SQL-level equivalent — a corrected row re-marked awaiting by any future/routing-regressed call site would allow correction_cycles=2 and a second correction.
recommended_fix: Add 'AND correction_cycles = 0' to mark_awaiting_correction.sql (and exhaust_reference_call.sql) so the one-cycle rule is structural, mirroring the taken_over_at guards.
